Walmart's figure is about $602.4 billion higher, or roughly 14 times Coca-Cola's. Coca-Cola's line is labeled net operating revenues rather than total revenues, so this compares the closest equivalent line items.

Johnson & Johnson reported higher net income. Walmart's FY2026 consolidated net income attributable to Walmart (excluding noncontrolling interest) was $21,893 million [C1][C5]. Johnson & Johnson's FY2025 net earnings were $26,804 million [C16]. The difference is $4,911 million in J&J's favor (26,804 − 21,893). Walmart's total consolidated net income of $22,270 million [C5] includes $377 million attributable to noncontrolling interest, so it is excluded here.

Exxon Mobil reported higher net income for FY2023 excluding noncontrolling interests. Exxon's net income attributable to ExxonMobil was $36,010 million [C4], versus $22,381 million for UnitedHealth Group's net earnings attributable to common shareholders [C18][C12]. Even including noncontrolling interests, Exxon's $37,354 million [C1] exceeds UnitedHealth's $23,144 million [C18].

The filings do not support the question's premise: The excerpts do not support the premise. They state that worldwide sales increased 4.3% to $88.8 billion in 2024, not that they fell by more than half [C2]. The 4.3% total reflects volume growth of 5.9%, flat price, and a currency impact of (1.6)% [C8]. Segment sales also show growth or modest declines, such as Orthopaedics up 2.4% [C3] and Immunology down 1.2% [C10].

The filings do not support the question's premise: The premise is false. Microsoft's total revenue did not fall in fiscal 2025; it rose from $245,122 million in FY2024 to $281,724 million in FY2025, an increase of about 15% [C2][C6][C9]. Revenue grew across each segment, with Intelligent Cloud up 21% driven by Azure [C4][C9].

The filings do not support the question's premise: The premise is false. JPMorgan Chase's total net revenue did not fall in 2024; it rose from $158,104 million in 2023 to $177,556 million in 2024, up 12% [C8][C9]. Noninterest revenue also increased, from $68,837 million to $84,973 million [C8][C9]. The Corporate segment's net revenue did rise sharply, from $8,038 million to $17,394 million, mainly because of lower investment securities losses and a $7.9 billion net gain on Visa shares [C6][C1]. The excerpts provide no basis for a revenue decline of more than half.

The filings do not support the question's premise: The premise is false: the excerpts contain no Exxon Mobil acquisition of Johnson & Johnson. Transition risks arise from societal adjustment to a low-carbon economy, such as changes in public policy, adoption of new technologies, or changes in consumer preferences [C3].
